deviations: Knesset sites (knesset.gov.il, fs.knesset.gov.il) redirect from this location to a geo-block page, and Nevo now requires login. Texts came from the Internet Archive captures named in the sheet, plus a capture of the 1984 gazette PDF for seq 22 (20220618013651, via the link on Wikisource). Government composition came from the English Wikipedia articles on the 18th, 20th, 22nd, 24th, 25th and 26th governments, as the sheet allows when the Knesset site is unreachable.

Reading dates came from Knesset database tables mirrored by Open Knesset outside the laws/ folder the sheet names: bills/kns_bill, plenum/kns_plmsessionitem, plenum/kns_plenumsession, knesset/kns_status, plenum/kns_documentplenumsession, bills/kns_documentbill. I treated them as Knesset records. They show agenda listings by bill status, not vote outcomes. 'First reading' means a sitting where the bill was listed with status 111 (for plenum discussion toward first reading). Where two such sittings straddle the 30-day threshold (seq 31, 35, 39), expedited is left blank.

Context for seq 42 and seq 48 (the earlier wording of the amended sections of the 1968 and 1992 Basic Laws: The Government) came from the Internet Archive captures of the Nevo pages the sheet lists (btl0630, btl0631).

Final-reading protocols: only two of eleven sittings are archived, 28.2.1984 (10_ptm_236481.DOC, seq 22) and 23.7.1991 (12_ptm_531826.PDF, seq 31), and neither names voters. All other final-vote and first-reading protocol files listed in Open Knesset's kns_documentplenumsession returned 'not archived'. Bill booklets with explanatory notes were archived only for seq 39 (13_ls1_292333.PDF); those for seq 19, 25, 28, 35, 42, 45, 48 and 51 were not.

Because no surviving record names the voters, coalition_only is blank for all eleven rows. For seq 22 and seq 31 the tallies are recorded, but a show-of-hands or electronic total cannot show whether any opposition member voted for.

The Internet Archive was intermittently 'Temporarily Offline' and refused connections; fetches were retried. A test of PDFKit, textutil and Vision OCR showed that Hebrew OCR is unavailable, so the image-only 1981 protocol could not have been read even had it been archived (it was not).

Press: one search of JTA for the 1984 vote and one general search for the 1981 amendment found no tally. The session's web-search allowance was then exhausted, so no press search was run for seq 25-51. The NYU archive was checked by search; its plenum items are settlement-related debates and were not used.

Court-related material: the 1981 search and the JTA search returned snippets naming court cases (on ministerial removal and on party disqualification); I did not open those pages. The Wikisource headers for Basic Law: The Judiciary and Basic Law: The Government link to recent judgments on later amendments; I did not open those links. The seq 39 explanatory notes (a permitted source) say the bill responds to a recent majority High Court reading of the existing anti-defection provision. I used the notes only for the bill's stated purpose, did not open the judgment, and coded no variable from it.

Discrepancies with the batch list: seq 39 amends ss. 5(b1) and 34(b) of the 1968 law only, as the gazette text and Nevo confirm, although Wikisource also lists it under the 1992 law. Seq 42 amends s. 21(d) of the 1968 law and s. 36 of the 1992 law. Seq 48 also repeals Basic Law: The Government (Amendment No. 3) of 1996. Seq 51 also amends the Knesset Law (Number of Members in Committees) 1994. OCR or print errors: the seq 42 gazette footnote reads '1966' for 1996, and its bill-booklet number reads 2562 where Open Knesset and Nevo give 2362.
